<BEGIN_SHACL>
@prefix sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
@prefix rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt#> .
@prefix nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#> .

# Shape targeting all ships (benchmark entities)
nltl:ShipIceNavigationShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:targetClass nltl:ship ;
    sh:label "Ship – Ice navigation and salinity constraints (TRF‑015 clause 2.2)" ;
    sh:description """
    Implements the requirement:
    – When the ship is navigating in ice, the operating draught must not exceed the Upper Ice Waterline (UIWL).
    – The operating trim must not exceed the maximum permitted ice trim.
    – The salinity of the sea water along the intended route must be taken into account when loading the ship.
    """ ;
    
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Draught shall not exceed UIWL when navigating in ice
    # -------------------------------------------------
    sh:sparql [
        a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;
        sh:message "When navigating in ice the operating draught exceeds the Upper Ice Waterline draught." ;
        sh:select """
            SELECT $this ( ?operDraughtVal AS ?value )
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:navigatingInIce true .
                $this nltl:operatingDraught ?operDraught .
                $this nltl:upperIceWaterlineDraught ?uiwl .
                
                ?operDraught qudt:numericValue ?operDraughtVal .
                ?operDraught qudt:unit <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/M> .
                
                ?uiwl qudt:numericValue ?uiwlVal .
                ?uiwl qudt:unit <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/M> .
                
                FILTER ( ?operDraughtVal > ?uiwlVal )
            }
        """ ;
    ] ;
    
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Trim shall not exceed the maximum permitted ice trim when navigating in ice
    # -------------------------------------------------
    sh:sparql [
        a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;
        sh:message "When navigating in ice the operating trim exceeds the maximum permitted ice trim." ;
        sh:select """
            SELECT $this ( ?operTrimVal AS ?value )
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:navigatingInIce true .
                $this nltl:operatingTrim ?operTrim .
                $this nltl:maximumPermittedIceTrim ?maxTrim .
                
                ?operTrim qudt:numericValue ?operTrimVal .
                ?operTrim qudt:unit <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/M> .
                
                ?maxTrim qudt:numericValue ?maxTrimVal .
                ?maxTrim qudt:unit <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/M> .
                
                FILTER ( ?operTrimVal > ?maxTrimVal )
            }
        """ ;
    ] ;
    
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Salinity values must be present when navigating in ice
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # 3a – intended route sea‑water salinity
    sh:sparql [
        a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;
        sh:message "When navigating in ice the intended route sea‑water salinity is missing or has an invalid unit." ;
        sh:select """
            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:navigatingInIce true .
                FILTER NOT EXISTS {
                    $this nltl:intendedRouteSeaWaterSalinity ?salinity .
                    ?salinity qudt:numericValue ?val .
                    ?salinity qudt:unit <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#gramPerKilogramSalinityUnit> .
                }
            }
        """ ;
    ] ;
    
    # 3b – loading‑calculation sea‑water salinity
    sh:sparql [
        a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;
        sh:message "When navigating in ice the loading‑calculation sea‑water salinity is missing or has an invalid unit." ;
        sh:select """
            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:navigatingInIce true .
                FILTER NOT EXISTS {
                    $this nltl:loadingCalculationSeaWaterSalinity ?salCalc .
                    ?salCalc qudt:numericValue ?val .
                    ?salCalc qudt:unit <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#gramPerKilogramSalinityUnit> .
                }
            }
        """ ;
    ] .
<END_SHACL>

The salinity of the sea water along the intended route shall be taken into account when loading the ship."

We need to encode constraints:

- When navigatingInIce true, operatingDraught must be <= upperIceWaterlineDraught (or not exceed UIWL; maybe also lower ice waterline? The clause says "draught and trim, limited by the UIWL, must not be exceeded when the ship is navigating in ice." So draught (operatingDraught) should be <= UIWL. Also trim must not exceed maximum permitted ice trim (maximumPermittedIceTrim). The clause also mentions "The salinity of the sea water along the intended route shall be taken into account when loading the ship." That possibly means loadingCalculationSeaWaterSalinity must be equal to intendedRouteSeaWaterSalinity? Or must be considered; we can enforce that loadingCalculationSeaWaterSalinity has same unit and maybe equal? Possibly a rule that a value is present (non-null) when loading. But cannot infer specifics. So we can require that if navigatingInIce true, both intendedRouteSeaWaterSalinity and loadingCalculationSeaWaterSalinity must be present (i.e., have values). And maybe they must be of type QuantityValue with unit gramPerKilogramSalinityUnit. Also ensure they are numbers.

We need to use quantityEncoding numeric_predicate and unit_predicate as declared: numeric_predicate = http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/numericValue, unit_predicate = http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/unit.

Thus for a property like operatingDraught, which is an ObjectProperty linking benchmarkEntity to QuantityValue. The quantity node should have qudt:numericValue and qudt:unit. We need to express constraints with sh:property shapes maybe targeting nodes of type ship (benchmarkEntity subclass). The owner class is ship.

We must not invent ownership beyond declared termOwners; they are all "ship". So targetClass ship.

Create a sh:NodeShape with sh:targetClass ship.

Define sh:property for each relevant property.

- For navigatingInIce: datatype boolean, requirement perhaps must be true? Actually condition only applies when navigatingInIce true; we need conditional constraints (sh:if). SHACL has sh:if and sh:then? There is sh:condition? Actually SHACL 1.1 has sh:if & sh:then via sh:Rule? Not standard. But we can use sh:property with sh:path navigatingInIce and sh:hasValue true? That would enforce it always true, which is not right. Better to use sh:or with conditional? Could use sh:property with sh:path operatingDraught and sh:maxCount etc, but need conditional gating.

Simplify: Create two separate shapes: one shape for navigationInIce true require draught limit, another shape for when property is true, but cannot express condition without SPARQL? We can use sh:property with sh:path [sh:or...] not ideal.

In SHACL, you can use sh:property with sh:nodeKind sh:Literal, sh:datatype etc. For conditional we can use sh:sparql constraint.

We'll use sh:SPARQLConstraint to express: FILTER (?navInIce = true) implies constraints. So include a sh:property? Actually sh:SPARQLConstraint at shape level.

Define shape with targetClass ship and a sh:sparql constraint that checks:

- If ?this <navigatingInIce> true, then ensure ?this <operatingDraught> ?draught, ?this <upperIceWaterlineDraught> ?uiwl, and numericValue(?draught) <= numericValue(?uiwl). Also ensure unit matches M.

- Also for trim: ?this <operatingTrim> ?trim, ?this <maximumPermittedIceTrim> ?maxTrim, numericValue(?trim) <= numericValue(?maxTrim).

- Also ensure salinity: if navigatingInIce true, the loadingCalculationSeaWaterSalinity and intendedRouteSeaWaterSalidity must exist, and their numeric values are maybe considered but we just enforce that they are present and have unit gramPerKilogramSalinityUnit.

Implement SPARQL with SELECT ?this WHERE { FILTER... } generating violation if condition fails. SHACL recommends using SELECT causing validation result for each result.

Similarly for trim:

sh:select ... where navigatingInIce true, trim > maxTrim.

And salinity presence:

SELECT $this WHERE {
  $this <navigatingInIce> true .
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { $this <intendedRouteSeaWaterSalinity> ?i . ?i <qudt:numericValue> ?iVal . ?i <qudt:unit> <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#gramPerKilogramSalinityUnit> . }
  UNION

}

But simpler: separate two constraints each ensuring existence.

Use sh:property with sh:path intendedRouteSeaWaterSalinity, sh:minCount 1, sh:nodeKind sh:IRI or sh:BlankNode? Actually property leads to QuantityValue node; we can enforce count with sh:minCount 1 (but only when navigatingInIce true). Use SPARQL again.
